entries.description: Reproduced: the classify-against-HomeHealthCare COM test timed out at 240s in both the batch run and a targeted retry during the prior set's re-measurement (2026-06-01); persistent and deterministic.

Static analysis of OleDbValueSampler + IR-based query-volume bound. Findings: (1) the OLE DB connection is opened ONCE and reused for the whole scan -- connection-per-call hypothesis RULED OUT. (2) Per non-key data column the sampler runs 3 queries: null-count, cardinality via COUNT(*) over a SELECT DISTINCT subquery (no index help on Jet/ACE -- prime suspect), and a TOP-200 value sample; plus 1 COUNT(*) per table. (3) Harvested HomeHealthCare IR has only 13 tables / 93 columns (~292 queries) -- the spec's 'hundreds of tables' claim is UNVERIFIED/likely wrong, so the cost is per-query (the DISTINCT cardinality on larger tables), not raw query volume. Remaining: a per-phase timed run to attribute wall-clock and quantify magnitude before fix-vs-quarantine is chosen.
